messages:
molly hart: DeployBot recommends auto-rollback for v2.15.0 due to a serialization mismatch hitting a small percentage of dedicated customers. Suggest we hold for triage for 10m.
dev ops: We saw mismatches in cached objects after a change to proto schema. Rolling back binary immediately will leave cache entries unreadable.
deploy-bot: DeployBot: Canary breach: error-rate 2.8% on /v1/embeddings (v2.15.0). Recommend auto-rollback to v2.14.9.
kevin kwan: Ops plan: 1) apply operator override to stop auto-rollback 2) pin traffic for dedicated customers in affected region to v2.14.9 3) deploy a compatibility shim (v2.15.0-shim) that attempts new proto, falls back to old. If shim fails in 12m then manual rollback + cache-migration.
molly hart: Pin command for ops: `routectl set-weight --route dedicated-eu --version v2.14.9 --weight 100 --match-header "X-Customer-Type: dedicated"`
dev ops: Hotfix artifact v2.15.0-shim built. Small try/catch around deserialize. Pushing to 3% test-slice.
deploy-bot: Note: auto-rollback scheduled in 5m. Operator override required to cancel.
kevin kwan: Operator override applied. Test-slice metrics: errors down from 2.8% to 0.4%.
molly hart: Customer note draft: "We detected errors for dedicated customers in EU after today's release. We pinned traffic to the prior stable release for affected customers and deployed a compatibility patch. We'll follow up with monitoring updates."
oncall-bot: Incident logged: INC-2150, severity: P2, mitigation: routing pin + compatibility shim; follow-up: postmortem and release-note update assigned.
kevin kwan: Decision: no immediate rollback. Monitor 30m, keep pin active, be ready to run manual rollback + cache-migrate if error rate rebounds. Closing when postmortem link added.
